title: fix(lint)!: the save door refuses a flow written into a package whose trigger object is outside that package's closure (#24669)
body:
Fixes #24669

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

Under a package closure the runtime save door states, a flow whose trigger object is outside that closure is now **refused**: `422 INVALID_METADATA`, one `flow-trigger-unknown-object` issue at `error`, at either position the rule reads (`config.objectName` on a `record-*` start node, or `config.timeRelative.object`). The dataset door (`object-reference-unknown`) and the view door (`list-view-object-outside-closure`) already give this verdict for the same reference under the same closure, so one mistake now gets one answer at all three doors (ruling #9612). A `sys_` name is still not judged.

With no closure stated, the advisory is byte-identical to before. That covers the three CLI commands, a write that names no package, the `sys_metadata` sentinel, and a package the registry cannot produce. Drafts stay ungated, and a stored row is judged at its next publish.

## Step 1: the census (triage `6279216806`'s first act, measured before any code)

**Method.** I parsed, with the TypeScript compiler API, every `.ts` / `.tsx` / `.mts` file in this repository at `a43405d596` (this branch's base) that contains a `type: 'start'` literal: 379 files and 930 start nodes. I read each start node's `config.objectName`, `config.triggerType` and `config.timeRelative.object`. 136 start nodes carry a record trigger (a `record-*` token, or a non-literal one) or a time-relative descriptor.

**Outside tests: 21 hits, 0 outside their package's closure.** Each trigger object is defined by the same single-package example stack (`com.example.showcase` / `com.example.todo`): `showcase_task` ×12 (one of them a sweep), `showcase_project` ×3, `showcase_expense_report` ×2, and `showcase_field_zoo`, `showcase_announcement`, `showcase_invoice` and `todo_task` ×1 each.

**Zero flows** in:
- `packages/apps/**`, `packages/platform-objects/**`, `packages/plugins/**`, `packages/services/**`;
- the `create-objectstack` blank template (its `src/flows/index.ts` is `export {};`);
- `examples/app-multi-package` (the one multi-package example), `examples/app-crm` (one screen flow, no trigger), `examples/embed-objectql`;
- any YAML/JSON flow file.

The `os g flow` scaffold binds `--object` or the stack's only object, so it stays in-stack by construction.

**`packages/qa/**`.** Every dogfood fixture's trigger object is declared by the same fixture stack. I resolved the 13 constant-named ones by hand. The upgrade-harness SQL holds only run records of showcase flows on `showcase_task`.

**Tests.** 115 trigger-bearing start nodes:
- 47 bind an object the same file declares, and 36 bind a computed name;
- 30 bind a name the file does not declare: unit tests that build engine stacks with no package, plus the deliberate CLI advisory pin `validate-flow-trigger-readiness.test.ts` (`other_package_object` → `billing_invoice`), which is unchanged;
- 1 binds `sys_user`, and 1 has no object.

The fixtures that write a flow into a package through the real door are the ones the consumer sweep surfaced (below).

**objectui** (read-only, at `32b492b67`): zero record-triggered or time-relative flow metadata outside tests. `apps/console/src/preview-samples.ts` holds one schedule-start preview sample, and nothing in it is written to a server.

**Verdict: no real writer**, so step 2's first branch applies and the code was written. Deployed rows were not measured.

## Premises

- **P1. Holds** at `a43405d596`. `validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts:446` / `:448` (record trigger) and `:498` / `:500` (time-relative): `severity: 'warning'`, keyed on `!objectNames.has(objectName) && !objectName.startsWith('sys_')`, not on the closure.
- **P2. Holds: a severity choice, not a new lookup.**
  - The flow rule is its own registry entry (`authoring-rules.ts`, `validateFlowTriggerReadiness`, `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['flow']`). It is not a reference-integrity-suite member, and its `run` callback did not read the rule context.
  - `buildRuntimeWriteSnapshotSet` narrows `objects` for every write type, flow included (`runtime-gate.ts:721`, `narrowObjectsToPackageClosure`). `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` puts `packageScope` on the rule context exactly when `packageScopeInForce` holds (`:1121`). So under a package write, `objectNames` already IS the closure.
  - The change hands `ctx.packageScope` to the rule and picks `error` when it is stated. `runtime-gate.ts` is unchanged. `reference-integrity-suite.ts` is touched only for one comment, after #24789 landed.
- **P3. Holds: an advisory at the runtime door, through the real `saveMetaItem`.**
  - Before, on `origin/main` `a43405d596` with lint built from it, `protocol.package-closure-gate.test.ts` and `protocol-publish-drafts-closure.test.ts` were 15/15 green. That included "reports a reference into a package the written one never declared": a flow written into `com.acme.crm` triggering on a `com.other.analytics` object answered `success: true` with `advisories = ['flow-trigger-unknown-object']`. The same body with no package drew nothing, because the stranger's object is in the whole collection.
  - With the rule changed and those pins untouched: 3 red. Two read `flow/crm_on_stranger failed author-time validation: 1 issue — flows[0].nodes[0].config.objectName [flow-trigger-unknown-object]`, and the third is the batch case in `protocol-publish-drafts-closure.test.ts`.

## What changes

- **`packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts`.** `validateFlowTriggerReadiness(stack, options = {})` takes an optional `{ packageScope }`. Both unknown-object sites go through one helper. With no closure, the finding is the old advisory (same keys, same order, same strings). Under a closure, the same id is `error`, with a message that names the package and its closure, and a hint that names the remedy (declare the dependency in the manifest `dependencies`, or set the named key to an in-closure object). The header's Severity section says why the hedge is gone under a closure.
- **`packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`.** The flow entry runs `validateFlowTriggerReadiness(stack, ctx.packageScope ? { packageScope: ctx.packageScope } : {})`. The `AuthoringRuleContext.packageScope` doc names its two readers.
- **`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`.** `os explain flow-trigger-unknown-object` said "at the runtime publish gate it is a save advisory … never a refusal", which this change makes false. It now gives the closure case, its remedy, and the draft and stored-row rules.
- **Comments made false by this change:** `validate-list-view-field-refs.ts` (two lines) and `reference-integrity-suite.ts` (one line, after #24789 landed), plus one sentence in `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`.
- **`.changeset/24669-flow-trigger-out-of-closure.md`:** `@objectstack/lint` `minor`, a `!` title, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, FROM / TO / Fix, the stored-row sentence, and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. `.changeset/pre.json` reads `mode: exit`, `tag: next`, so the next version pass cuts 18.0.0 and this ships in it. The changeset says so.

## Pins

- **Lint** (`runtime-gate.package-closure.test.ts`, through `runRuntimeAuthoringRules`). The new block, for both positions:
  - an undeclared package's object is refused at the key, with a hint naming the package and `dependencies`;
  - an object that exists nowhere is refused;
  - admitted: the own package, a declared dependency, `isSystem` objects (one of them stranger-owned), a carried `sys_` object, a `sys_` name the snapshot does not carry, and a provenance-less overlay row;
  - with no package, or an empty package id: the stranger's object is clean, and the ghost is advised. The door's severity, message and hint equal the CLI's byte for byte;
  - the CLI reading is unchanged.

  The three existing flow pins in that file now assert severity: "a REAL finding survives narrowing" (same rule and path, advisory on the whole collection, refused under the closure), the undeclared case, and the stored-sibling case.
- **Protocol** (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.package-closure-gate.test.ts`, through the real `saveMetaItem` / `publishMetaItem`):
  - refused `422 INVALID_METADATA`, asserting the ADR-0112 `code` + `status`, the issue's `severity` / `path` and the hint, with nothing stored. This holds for `config.objectName`, `config.timeRelative.object`, and an object that exists nowhere;
  - admitted at both positions: the own package, a declared dependency, an `isSystem` platform object and `sys_user`;
  - the draft save of the refused body succeeds and stores no active row, and its promotion is refused;
  - with no package, the ghost keeps its `warning` advisory at both positions;
  - the uninstalled-package case narrows nothing and resolves.

## Fixtures the consumer sweep found (outside `packages/lint` / `packages/spec`), for the seat's #6367 addendum

All four are test files only. There is no `protocol.ts` or `objectql` source change, and no assertion was weakened.

1. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.package-closure-gate.test.ts`: the protocol-layer pin block above. Its advisory pins are re-pinned to the refusal.
2. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-publish-drafts-closure.test.ts`: "STILL reports a flow bound to an object that is in neither the batch nor the registry" becomes "STILL refuses". The batch fails, the ghost-triggered flow is `INVALID_METADATA` with the issue at `error`, and the healthy sibling is `BATCH_ABORTED`.
3. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.publish-item-rebind-announce.test.ts`: the fixture is re-trued. Its stub registry now lists the flows' trigger object `ticket` under the package `app.ops`. The batch CONTROL case had gone red because `ticket` was outside the closure. Assertions are unchanged.
4. `packages/objectql/src/protocol-duplicate-package-unprefixed-object.test.ts`: "a name already claimed is refused up front" is re-pinned to three refusals. With the `ticket` copy refused, the copied `dupsrc_on_ticket` keeps the source's `ticket` as its trigger object, which is outside the copy package's closure, so the flow door refuses it. This is the same shape as #24630's view re-pin (the seat's answer A, `6277565064`). The changeset's door list names `duplicatePackage`.

## Ablation (G5): run once, recorded here, no permanent file

The fix was committed first. `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs --hold`, armed with a `trap` restore, replaced the closure branch's `severity: 'error',` with `severity: 'warning',` plus a dist-visible marker.
- Mutate leg: anchor 1 → 0, blob `48415eb218` → `255f3f2863`. `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs @objectstack/lint ABLATION_24669` found the marker in 4 built files.
- The lint pins went red: 8 of 36. So did the protocol pins: 6 of 20, every refusal case (objectName, timeRelative, ghost, draft promotion, uninstalled control, batch). The direction was red, as expected.
- Restore leg: blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, whole tree clean. After a rebuild, `--absent` found the marker in none of the 20 built files. Both files went green again: 36/36 and 20/20.

## Verification

- **Consumer sweep** (`--maxWorkers=2`, under `os-verify-lock.sh`), on `aa20228392`. Results: `lint` 6953/6953; `service-automation` 2605; `runtime` 7587 (19 skipped); `rest` 6404 (344 skipped). The two first-run reds were fixtures 3 and 4 above, re-run green after re-truing: `metadata-protocol` was 1 red of 20834, and `objectql` 1 red of 8495. `cli --project unit` was 4612 passed, with 2 suites refused for a missing prerequisite (`packages/cli is not built`), not a measurement. Both re-ran green after a cli build, below.
- **After merging `origin/main` (#24789 landed), on `009a2b2b09`.** Results: `lint` full suite and `typecheck` green; `metadata-protocol` full suite green; the objectql fixture green; the two cli suites green. `metadata-protocol` `typecheck` was green on the pre-merge head.
- **Gates, on the final head `3d4226ca4f`.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (no paths) derives 96 families. All 96 ran with their exit codes recorded, and `--ran` reconciles them: "96 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 96 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero …)". 95 exit 0. One is red **by design**: `check-empty-changeset --base origin/main` (exit 1, the next section). On the `009a2b2b09` pass, `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first exited 3 (missing prerequisite: dist absent). They re-ran green after the missing packages were built, and both are exit 0 in the final-head pass.
- **`test:repo`:** not run locally. Nothing in its project changed, and CI's `Test Core` runs it.

## A pending release note corrected: please confirm (`Check Changeset` stays red by design)

`.changeset/24563-list-view-out-of-closure.md` (#24563's, unreleased) said under **Unchanged**: "The flow door: `flow-trigger-unknown-object` stays an advisory." This PR makes that sentence false, so the line now reads: "The flow door: under the same closure, `flow-trigger-unknown-object` refuses an out-of-closure trigger object too (#24669, see that changeset)." This is check-empty-changeset's DELIBERATE CORRECTION class. Per ruling D, the gate stays red, and the correction needs written confirmation here. `Check Changeset` is not a required context.

## File surface beyond the claim

The claim named the rule file, the closure plumbing, the lint pins, one changeset, and the riders. I also touched the following, each because this change made a sentence in it false:
- `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`: the `os explain` text;
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`: one sentence. Its lines are disjoint from #24789's hunk, and the merge was clean;
- `packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.ts`: two comment lines;
- `packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts`: one comment line, after #24789 landed;
- `.changeset/24563-list-view-out-of-closure.md`: one line, after #24789 landed.

Before touching these, I read the file lists of all open PRs. Only #24789 overlapped, and it has since landed.

## Acceptance notes

- **Not measured: Studio's flow designer object picker** (objectui). I did not check whether it offers objects outside the package's closure when you author inside a package. If it does, an author can now pick an object the publish refuses. That refusal is loud and names the fix, and the view door has the same shape. This is an observation only; no carrier is named.
- **Deployed stored rows were not measured.** A stored flow with an out-of-closure trigger keeps loading and firing. It is refused only at its next publish, and the refusal names the fix.
